headline: A wheel in stone. A world in motion.
opening: Look closely at the wheel. Its rim holds another pattern, and that pattern asks for another look. At Konark, the pleasure is in slowing down enough to notice.
opening_kind: Original narration grounded in the photograph; not an eyewitness account.

history.heading: Built for the sun
history.text: Narasimha Deva I’s 13th-century temple imagines Surya’s chariot in stone. Its principal tower no longer survives; the standing audience hall and roofless dance hall belong to a larger complex. Knowing what has been lost changes how you look at what remains.

culture_heading: A poem, a legend, a stage
culture_intro: Read the story that grew around the stones, then seek the living arts that gather beside them.

surprise.heading: The wheel is only the beginning.

metrics.label: carved wheels in the chariot design

surprise.text: UNESCO describes reliefs of musicians, dancers and animals across the temple. Look beyond the silhouette: the small figures make this stone world feel inhabited.
surprise.reveal: Choose one carved figure and describe its posture before asking a guide about it. This is our observation prompt, not a claim that every carving has one agreed meaning.

belief.label: Local legend · a literary retelling
belief.heading: The boy who completed the temple
belief.text: In the Dharmapada tradition discussed by Snigdha Acharya in Odisha Review, the young son of craftsman Bisu Moharana completes the temple’s difficult final work. The story ends with the boy’s death and lives on as a tale of sacrifice.
belief.qualification: This is a legend, not verified construction history. Gopabandhu Das’s poem Dharmapada is one literary route into the story.

invitation.heading: Choose one detail to carry home
invitation.text: A carved spoke, a dancer’s gesture, a line of shadow. Which small detail would you draw on a postcard?
invitation.kind: Editorial observation prompt; no answer collection.
